title: A puddle after rain
goal: Use repeated observations of one location to describe change while recognising limits of the measurement.
evidence: Student distinguishes a shorter puddle from a measured volume loss and proposes a way to improve evidence.
lesson: After rainfall observation; revisit safely with teacher and compare class records.
brief: Field record C. Heading 'What changed at our puddle?' Method 'Same puddle • same marked line • no new rain'. Table 'Time | Width along the line' '9 am | 80 cm', '1 pm | 45 cm'. Two small overhead observation sketches of broad vs narrower puddle, dashed measurement line across each, caption 'Sketches, not to scale'. Blank 'Our observation' and 'A possible explanation'. Prompt 'Did we measure the amount of water?' with empty 'What should we check next?' Save field record plus photo/sketch/voice. Never show 35 cm as supplied answer or label width as water volume.
